description.summary: an allow/deny prompt for privileged requests

protocol.description:
Lets a privileged, compositor-trusted client (in practice, this compositor's own xdg-desktop-portal backends) ask that an "app X wants to do Y" prompt be shown to the user, and report back their answer.
This is deliberately not exposed to ordinary clients: the manager global is only advertised to clients connected through the compositor's privileged capture socket (see `crate::screencopy`), the same channel used for `ext-image-capture-source-v1`/`ext-image-copy-capture-v1`. A prompt only ever names an `app_id` and a human-readable reason chosen by the trusted caller, never anything the prompted-about app itself can influence directly.
The prompt itself is always drawn and answered by the compositor - there is deliberately no way for any client, privileged or not, to take over rendering it or to answer on the user's behalf. An earlier version of this protocol let a second privileged role (a *renderer*, in practice this compositor's companion shell) do exactly that; it was removed because the only thing gating who could claim that role was "connected through the same privileged socket", which every client on this system can do - letting any local process silently self-approve every prompt, its own included, with no UI ever shown. See `crate::permission_prompt`'s module doc for the fallback prompt this compositor draws itself.

interface.name: ironland_permission_prompt_manager_v1
interface.description: This interface allows a privileged client to ask that a permission prompt be shown to the user.

request.name: prompt
request.description: Queues a prompt for display. If another prompt is already showing, this one waits its turn. Exactly one of `allowed`/`denied` is sent to the returned object once the user answers.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: requesting application id, shown to the user

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: human-readable description of what's being requested

request.name: choose_output

description.summary: ask the user to pick one monitor

request.description:
Queues a monitor chooser: the compositor shows a panel listing its outputs (numbered left to right) and marks every monitor with the same number in its top-left corner, so the user can tell which is which. Exactly one of `chosen`/`cancelled` is sent to the returned object once the user answers. Waits behind any showing permission prompt, and behind earlier choosers.
Like `prompt`, this is drawn and answered by the compositor itself; the requester only learns the answer.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: requesting application id, shown to the user

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: human-readable description of what's being requested

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying the manager doesn't affect prompts already created through it.

description.summary: a queued or showing permission prompt

event.name: allowed
event.description: Sent at most once, when the user answers yes.

event.name: denied

description.summary: the user denied the request, or the prompt was cancelled

event.description: Sent at most once, when the user answers no, or when the prompt is destroyed by the compositor before being answered (e.g. session teardown).

request.name: destroy
request.description: If not yet answered, this cancels it (dismissing it from the queue, or from the screen if it was showing) with no `allowed`/`denied` event sent for it.

description.summary: a queued or showing monitor chooser

event.name: chosen
event.description: Sent at most once. `name` is the output's name, the same string its `wl_output.name` event (version 4) carries.

event.name: cancelled

description.summary: the user cancelled, or the chooser was torn down

event.description: Sent at most once, when the user dismisses the chooser or the compositor tears it down before it was answered.

request.name: destroy
request.description: If not yet answered, this cancels it (dismissing it from the queue, or from the screen if it was showing) with no `chosen`/`cancelled` event sent for it.
